premises: High configurational entropy and atomic size mismatch create high diffusion barriers in multi-element near-equiatomic nanoparticles.
These high diffusion barriers kinetically stabilize the uniform solid-solution phase at lower temperatures.
Above a critical temperature threshold, thermal energy overcomes these barriers, triggering rapid diffusion, segregation, and phase separation.
This kinetic stabilization mechanism is supported by prior MC+MD simulations showing sluggish diffusion and uniform elemental distribution at 773 K.
In situ TEM heating experiments can monitor atomic diffusion and structural evolution as a function of temperature.
